recipes.name: Golden Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 2 (10.75 ounce) cans condensed golden mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Rinse pork chops, pat dry, and season with seasoned salt and pepper. Place them in a 9x13 inch baking dish. In a separate small bowl, combine the onion, mushrooms and soup. Mix together well and spoon over the chops.

Cover, and bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 45 minutes. Uncover, and bake for 15 more minutes. (Note: Time could be less or more depending on the thickness of the chops.) Pork chops are done when their internal temperature has reached 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Golden Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: This is so yummy, I never make enough. Seasoned pork chops are smothered in a golden mushroom sauce and baked with fresh mushroom slices and onion.

review.reviewBody: This was pretty good. Everyone in my family really liked it. I hate it when people make a million changes in a review but.... I did saute the onion, (canned) mushrooms and about a tablespoon of minced(jar)garlic in a skillet until soft, removed it from the skillet and put in a bowl. I browned the pork chops in the same skillet, seasoning them with a good amount of season salt, garlic powder and pepper while in the skillet, transferred to the baking pan and topped with onion mixture and soup. Very flavorfull and tender, I will definitley make again.

I prefer not to review if I had to make a change but I did want to share my experience. I made this as written except that I only had 1 can of golden mushroom so I did have to substitute a can of cream of mushroom. I added 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce and 1 tbsp ketchup to the cream of mushroom soup. It was delicious. I do think it would be even better with all golden mushroom. UPDATE: I made this with 1 can of golden mushroom soup and added an envelope of pork gravy mix and a big dollop of sour cream ( maybe 1/4 x1/2 cup). I sautéd chopped onion and fresh mushrooms and put that over the chops and gravy. Baked as directed. This kicked it up a notch and made it taste a bit different. Still love the original recipe.

Very similar to what I’ve been making for eons. It really is yummy - DH adores. 😉 Don’t use onion at all but lots of Cremini sliced mushrooms. Center cut loin chops browned with S+P and Rosemary. Into casserole on bottom, covered with sliced mush. Soup 1 can - mixed with a 1 can of whipping cream and into the oven for an hour. Makes a fantastic gravy! Just 🙏 they continue making the GMS! Great reviews and no wonder! White/Wild Rice and Steamed Broccoli. Yes! 😋

I make this frequently in my slow cooker and we love it. I pretty much stick to the recipe, other than that I coat the chops liberally with seasoning salt and pepper, no measuring. I put half the soup mixture in the bottom of the cooker, add the chops then spread the rest of the soup on top. I cook on Low for 8 hours and we end up with the most flavorful, tender pork chops ever. If I want gravy, I remove the chops and stir a roux into the the soup. Perfect!

I have made this almost to the Tee ( even before I came across this recipe )
 I did like most, seasoned the chops with salt & pepper, a little thyme, and garlic powder. I did a hot quick sear on the stove first. after removing the meat, place it in a baking dish and quickly into the oven. 
 sauté the onions, fresh minced garlic, and mushrooms (I like shiitake mushrooms) in the same pan. add the mushroom soup just to blend and pour over the chops. cover and bake for 30 minutes at 375° (may vary depending on thickness of the chops). 
I have served this w mashed potatoes using the reserved "gravy", over Jasmine rice, and over egg noodles.
turned out perfectly juicy every time! everyone loved them !!

Simple and delicious, great weeknight family comfort food. I used a large oven safe saute pan, and seasoned my chops with Lawrey's and cracked black pepper, and browned on one side of the pan. The other side I added the onions and mushrooms, seasoned, and sauteed as well. When the chops were browned I just mixed everything together with the sauce, and placed the covered pan in the oven 350* for 45 minutes. Served with mashed potatoes and oven roasted asparagus. Hubs loved this meal. Thanks of sharing!

Use a deeper dish or better yet a foil pan for easy cleanup. My 6 chops were of medium thickness and I only used 1 can of Golden Mushroom soup and it boiled over just a bit. ( I always have some heavy duty aluminum foil on the bottom of my oven) I also added some fresh diced plum tomatoes along with the sliced mushrooms and a generous splash of white wine. Very simple recipe but the flavor of the sauce was really good. I would make this again.

AS written this recipe is only a 3. Browning the meat before baking makes a huge difference and is well worth the extra time and effort. I brown the meat in 2-3 batches in a cast iron skillet, deglaze the pan with a small amount of white wine, then add back all the ingredients, cover the skillet with foil and pop into the oven.

I will definitely make this again. The only ingredient change I made was to add a little Frank's Hot Sauce to the gravy. Also, I cooked it on low on the stovetop for about an hour and a half after browning the seasoned meat (I use Montreal Steak seasoning), onions, and mushrooms. It came out very tender. A pleasant change from recipes using Cream of Mushroom soup.
I made this for Christmas. My family loved them. I did saute the onions, mushrooms added fresh garlic then added them to the golden mushroom soup. I did brown the pork chops ahead of time.

Great recipe. I followed other reviewers' suggestions and used fresh mushrooms sautéed with onion & garlic in olive oil, and I browned the seasoned chops after removing the veggies. The whole family gave this recipe 5 stars. This definitely goes on our regular rotation of meals!

I followed the recipe mostly, I didn't have mushrooms tho. I seasoned the chops with Tony's Cajun seasoning & garlic powder, S&P. Put in a splash of Worsteshire sauce with the soup. I doubled the recipe with 12 boneless chops. Took 50 minutes total, only 5 min uncovered they were done. Awesome recipe, will make again!
We love this recipe! I added a can of cream of mushroom too, sliced up potatoes and mixed that in with the mushrooms and onions, and I top it with cheddar cheese!
This a delicious and simple recipe. I don’t bake it, just brown the chops, cover and simmer on low in the sauce. Much juicier that way
No changes. So easy and so delicious and tender.
Made as written and this was pretty good. 45 minutes was all the cook time mine needed. The flavors were great and the soup gave it that perfect gravy consistency.

The flavor is great. I sautéed the onion, garlic, and mushrooms per another review, and reduced the bake time to 30 minutes covered, 15 minutes uncovered, and my 1/2-inch thick, boneless porkchops were way over cooked. Definitely take the hint in Step 3 and check the temperature of the pork as it's cooking on this one if you want tender chops.

THe taste was OK but chops were tough as could be! It was good looking meat from a local grocery chain. I used to make a recipe similar to this and it was great, not sure what the problem was. I do think they may have been overcooked-were well done at 45 min. Probably won't make this again.
I have made this for years! We love it and always have to have mashed potatoes with it, this is total comfort dinner.

FANTASTIC! I made the recipe exactly as was called for, but sprinkled steak seasoning over the meat with the salt and pepper. I did not sautee the mushrooms and onions because they get sauteed plenty, while baking, and I did not want "mushy" veggies. It turned out GREAT! I cooked a side of rice in my rice maker, and we spooned the gravy from the casserole over the rice! This is a wonderful quick & easy meal!!!!! Thanks so much for this recipe!
